note: Curecanti NRA campground at the northwest end of the Soap Creek arm of Blue Mesa Reservoir, 7,880 ft, with wide views and solitude. Access is 7 miles of gravel Soap Creek Road (CR 721): passable to trailers and RVs when dry, impassable when wet. --Claude
summary: NPS campground record + conditions + rec.gov API/rates/catalog: confirmed $20 FCFS, vault toilets, electric 0, first-come. Changed count 29 -> 28 (NPS totalSites; rec.gov's 29th is a scan-and-pay placeholder). Added pull_through, no water/showers/dump, season May-October (typical), 14-night max. Note trimmed of count/toilets/FCFS restatements.
flags: Waterfront (stored lakeview): upgrade LEAD for the Lower loop only. On Esri imagery (low reservoir) the 5 Lower-loop sites (24, 26-29) sit on open ground right at the vegetation line above Blue Mesa's Soap Creek arm, roughly 20-40 m from the high-water edge, with a wide exposed drawdown band below; the Middle loop (16) is ~400 m from the arm's inlet and the Upper loop ~1.5 km. Needs the gate against Blue Mesa full pool (7,519 ft) vs the Lower loop's elevation.

Pin: stored 38.52571,-107.3149 is the NPS/rec.gov facility point, on the Upper loop (7 sites, horse corral). The 28 site points span three loops ~1 km apart (overall centroid 38.52324,-107.30756, 696 m away, falls between them). Suggest re-pinning to the Middle loop, the largest, at about 38.5238,-107.3061.

Site mix: NPS lists totalSites 28 with horse 2, tentOnly 10, walkBoatTo 10, rvOnly 0, which would leave few RV-usable sites, but rec.gov's catalog has no tent-only or walk-to type and the NPS text says 'Tents and medium sized RVs can be accommodated'. Probably stale NPS breakdown; not applied. No maximum length is published ('medium sized').

Season conflict: NPS 'Typically open May through October'; rec.gov's 2026 fee season is 2026-10-08 to 2026-11-16 (2025: 04-26 to 09-30). The conditions page currently (late October) lists Ponderosa open. Recorded the NPS typical May-October.
Access: Soap Creek Road advisory kept in the note ('During dry conditions, the first 7 miles of Soap Creek Road are passable to trailers and RVs. Rain can make the Soap Creek Road impassable.').
Phone: none stored. NPS and rec.gov both give (970) 641-2337 (Curecanti). Suggest adding.
Website: recreation.gov (scan-and-pay only); add the NPS page https://www.nps.gov/cure/planyourvisit/camp_ponderosa.htm.
Alert: Blue Mesa cyanotoxin advisory (2026-10-13: below state thresholds, keep kids and pets out of the water). Not a closure.
